# Story 16 — Tasks & Reminders

## Prerequisites

- Story 01 — Authentication & Login completed: current-user identification via `ClaimsPrincipalExtensions` in `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api/Auth/ClaimsPrincipalExtensions.cs` is available.
- Story 02 — Users Management completed: `User` entity in `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Domain/Users/User.cs` and `UsersController` are in place.
- Story 03 — Roles & Permissions completed: `Permissions` static registry in `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Domain/Roles/Permissions.cs`, `HasPermissionAttribute` in `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api/Authorization/HasPermissionAttribute.cs`, and seeding via `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Infrastructure/Persistence/DbSeeder.cs`.
- Story 15 — Agent Dashboard completed: the dashboard shell / route structure is available so Tasks & Reminders can be added as a sibling page under Agent Desk.

---

## Story Goal

Deliver a **Tasks & Reminders** section for the currently authenticated Agent, scoped strictly to personal tasks and their optional reminder timestamps. The Agent can create, view, edit, complete, and delete their own tasks; each task may carry a `reminderAt` date/time. The UI clearly distinguishes **completed**, **pending**, **upcoming reminder**, and **overdue reminder** states.

Out of scope (per intake): assigned-tickets dashboard, customer info panels, quick replies, team collaboration, notifications, SLA, escalation, reassignment, customer-portal tasks, analytics/reporting. Tasks are **not** linked to specific tickets or customers in this story; they are personal work items owned by the Agent.

## Product rules (from story)

- A **task** belongs to exactly one Agent (the authenticated user who created it). Only that Agent (and admins with elevated permissions, per the existing model) can read/update/delete/complete it.
- A task has a required **title**. Optional fields: **description**, **reminderAt** (UTC), **completedAt** (UTC, set on complete).
- **Reminder state** is derived server-side and re-computed client-side:
  - `completed` — `completedAt != null`.
  - `overdue` — not completed **and** `reminderAt != null` **and** `reminderAt < now (UTC)`.
  - `upcoming` — not completed **and** `reminderAt != null` **and** `reminderAt >= now`.
  - `pending` — not completed **and** `reminderAt == null`.
- **Delete** is permitted only when the current user is the owner (or has the delete permission).
- **Complete** is idempotent: re-completing does not change `completedAt`; re-opening (uncomplete) clears `completedAt`.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Empty task list** — the `TasksListPage` renders an empty-state block ("You have no tasks yet.") instead of an empty table. Backend `ListAsync` returns `[]` (never null).
- **No reminders set** — the reminders callout hides itself when both upcoming and overdue lists are empty.
- **Blank / whitespace-only title** — server rejects with 400 and a `title` field error; client shows inline validation and disables **Save**.
- **Title > 200 chars / description > 4000 chars** — server rejects with 400; client enforces the same limits with helper text.
- **`reminderAt` in the past on create** — allowed; item immediately renders as **Overdue** (per product rules). Do not silently discard.
- **Time zones** — server stores and returns UTC; client sends `new Date(local).toISOString()`. The `datetime-local` input has no timezone; convert in `TaskFormPage.tsx`.
- **Cross-agent access** — Agent A cannot read/edit/delete Agent B's task. Enforced by `.Where(t => t.OwnerUserId == currentUserId)` in `AgentTasksService`; verified by unit test.
- **Missing permission** — controller returns 403; nav entry hidden; page route redirects per `PermissionRoute.tsx` behaviour.
- **Concurrent complete + delete** — `CompleteAsync`/`DeleteAsync` handle "already deleted" as 404, not 500. Wrap `SaveChangesAsync` with the same error handling `CustomerNotesService.cs` uses.
- **Reopen a task that was never completed** — no-op returning the current DTO; do not throw.
- **User deletion** — cascade delete removes tasks (per FK config in step 3); document in the migration if the choice differs from `CustomerNote`'s cascade behaviour.
- **DST / clock skew** — server-side `State` is authoritative; client recomputes only for display refresh (e.g. minute-timer). Do not rely on client time to determine authorization or persistence.

## Migration / Rollback

- **Forward:** apply the new `AddAgentTasks` migration via `dotnet ef database update -p backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Infrastructure -s backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api`. Seeder (`DbSeeder.cs`) will insert new permission rows on next startup and grant them to the Agent role.
- **Half-applied state:** if the migration succeeded but the seeder did not run, the API will return 403 for all `/api/agent-desk/tasks` calls because the permissions do not exist yet — no data loss. Re-run the app so the seeder completes.
- **Rollback:** `dotnet ef migrations remove -p backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Infrastructure -s backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api` (before deploy), or `dotnet ef database update <PreviousMigrationName>` to revert. Also remove the seeded `agenttasks.*` permission rows and any `RolePermissions` linking them (idempotent cleanup script recommended if run in production).

## Correction (post-implementation) — Ticket-linked tasks, two creation entry points

Applied after the base story above shipped. Adds an **optional** `TicketId` to the existing `AgentTask`
model — every rule above (owner-only visibility, required title, idempotent complete/reopen, etc.)
is unchanged and still enforced exactly as written. Nothing here replaces or forks the task system;
it is the same model and the same create/update endpoints, just with one more optional field.

### Updated model

```
Task
├── Title
├── Description
├── Due Date / Reminder (ReminderAt)
├── Status (derived: Pending | Upcoming | Overdue | Completed)
├── Assigned Agent (OwnerUserId — the existing owner-scoping)
└── TicketId (optional, new)
```

### Two creation entry points

1. **From the Tasks & Reminders page** (`/agent-desk/tasks/new`) — an optional **Related ticket**
   dropdown lets the Agent pick any ticket from the list, or leave it as **— None —** for a general,
   unlinked task. `Tasks → Add Task → optionally select Ticket → Save`.
2. **From a ticket's detail page** (`/agent-desk/tasks/new?ticketId=<id>`) — the ticket is already
   known from the URL, so the form shows a **read-only** "Linked ticket" line instead of a dropdown;
   the Agent is never asked to select it again, and cannot change it away on this screen.
   `Ticket → Add Task → TicketId automatically set → Save`.

Editing an existing task (`/agent-desk/tasks/:id/edit`) always shows the dropdown, editable —
re-linking or unlinking (**— None —**) a task from its ticket after creation is allowed regardless of
which entry point originally created it.

### Backend changes

- `AgentTask.cs` — `Guid? TicketId` + `Ticket? Ticket` navigation. `Restrict` on delete, matching every
  other FK on `Ticket` (a ticket is never hard-deleted).
- Migration `AddAgentTaskTicketLink` — adds the nullable column, index, and FK only.
- `CreateAgentTaskRequest` / `UpdateAgentTaskRequest` gain an optional `TicketId` (defaults to `null`,
  so this is additive — no existing caller breaks). `AgentTaskDto` gains `TicketId` + a denormalized
  `TicketSubject` for display.
- A new `AgentTaskOperationOutcome.TicketNotFound` → `404 { "error": "ticket_not_found" }` when a
  caller supplies a `TicketId` that does not exist.
- `ListAsync` gains an optional `ticketId` filter — `GET /api/agent-desk/tasks?ticketId=<id>` is what
  powers the ticket detail page's Tasks section. It still filters to `OwnerUserId == currentUserId`
  first — **being ticket-linked never relaxes the owner-privacy boundary**: a task is only ever visible
  to the agent who owns it, whether or not it is also linked to a ticket other agents can see.

### Frontend changes

- `TasksListPage.tsx` — new **Ticket** column: a link to the ticket when linked, "General" otherwise.
- `TaskFormPage.tsx` — the dropdown/read-only-line split described above.
- `TicketTasksPanel.tsx` (new) — mounted on `TicketDetailPage.tsx` behind `agenttasks.read`, lists the
  *current viewer's own* tasks linked to that ticket with an "Add task" shortcut
  (`agenttasks.create`) that pre-fills `?ticketId=`.

### Updated acceptance criteria (additive to the Done Criteria above)

- [ ] Agent can create a task from the Tasks & Reminders page with no ticket selected (general task).
- [ ] Agent can create a task from the Tasks & Reminders page with a ticket selected from a dropdown.
- [ ] Agent can create a task directly from a ticket's detail page; the ticket is set automatically,
      with no dropdown/selection step.
- [ ] A task created from a ticket appears both in the Agent's Tasks & Reminders list and in that
      ticket's own Tasks section.
- [ ] The Tasks & Reminders list shows both general (unlinked) and ticket-linked tasks, with a visible
      reference to the related ticket for the latter.
- [ ] Task → Ticket navigation works (clicking the ticket reference opens the ticket).
- [ ] Ticket → Tasks navigation works (the ticket detail page lists its linked tasks).
- [ ] Creating a task with an unknown `TicketId` is rejected with `404 { error: "ticket_not_found" }`.
- [ ] A second Agent still cannot see a first Agent's tasks — linked or general — via any path,
      including the ticket-scoped list.
- [ ] All pre-existing Story 16 behavior (owner-scoping, idempotent complete/reopen, validation,
      audit logging) is unchanged and still passes its existing tests.
